In many of these studies, the meals were designed to disguise variation in fat level from participants. It is therefore possible that
effects on mood may have resulted from discrepancies between subjects' expectations of certain postingestive effects, and the actual
effects that resulted from neurohormonal responses to detection of speciﬁc nutrients in the duodenum and liver. A case in point
may be the increase in tension, 90 min postlunch, with increasing fat intake, reported by predominately female subjects: this might
reﬂect an aversive reaction to (unexpected) fat-related postingestive sensations.
